dataset: North Korea (DPRK) access and rules change log

entries.detail: The US State Department declared all US passports invalid for travel to, in, or through the DPRK unless specially validated. The restriction has been renewed every year since.

sources.name: US Department of State — Public Notice 13073, Federal Register

entries.title: US passports declared invalid for North Korea travel

entries.detail: Malaysia's Foreign Ministry banned all Malaysians from travelling to the DPRK until further notice, citing tensions on the Korean Peninsula. The ban remains in force.

sources.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Malaysia
Nikkei Asia

entries.title: Malaysia bans its citizens from travelling to North Korea

entries.detail: The DPRK sealed its borders in January 2020, suspending all foreign tourism. The closure lasted, with narrow exceptions, for more than five years.

sources.name: Uri Tours — Air Koryo and tourism updates
UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — North Korea travel advice

entries.title: North Korea closes its borders over COVID-19

entries.detail: As an exception to the closure, the DPRK began admitting tourists holding Russian citizenship, starting with group tours in February 2024. Russians remain the only nationality issued tourist visas.

sources.name: Korea Konsult — DPRK tourism status, October 2026
Uri Tours — Air Koryo service update, April 2026

entries.title: Russian tourist groups admitted — first tourists since 2020

entries.detail: The Rason Special Economic Zone in the northeast admitted Western tour groups (via Koryo Tours and Young Pioneer Tours) — the first non-Russian, non-Chinese tourists since 2020. US, South Korean and Japanese nationals were excluded.

sources.name: Korea JoongAng Daily
Young Pioneer Tours — November 2026 update

entries.title: Rason SEZ opens to Western tourists

entries.detail: DPRK authorities suspended access for all foreign nationals except Russians, with no official explanation. Tourism to Rason has not resumed.

sources.name: Young Pioneer Tours — November 2026 update
Uri Tours — Is North Korea open for tourism? FAQ

entries.title: Rason access suspended again after less than three weeks

entries.detail: About 200 foreign amateurs from some 46 countries ran the Pyongyang Marathon as an invited sporting delegation arranged with Koryo Tours — the first foreign participation in six years. Participants entered as athletes on special visas, not as tourists.

sources.name: Uri Tours — Is North Korea open for tourism? FAQ

entries.title: Pyongyang Marathon runs with foreign amateur runners

entries.detail: The Wonsan-Kalma Coastal Tourist Area on the Kalma Peninsula opened to visitors on 1 July 2025, a week after an opening ceremony attended by Kim Jong Un and the Russian ambassador. Initial visitors were domestic tourists.

sources.name: Korea Times — Russian agency promotes Kalma resort tours

entries.title: Wonsan-Kalma resort opens

entries.detail: Authorities announced the resort would no longer accept foreign tourists, without giving a reason. Russian group tours were the exception: they visited repeatedly in July 2025, and Russian operators sold Wonsan packages from August 2025.

sources.name: Yonhap News Agency
Korea Times

entries.title: Wonsan-Kalma stops accepting foreign tourists — Russians excepted

entries.detail: The 2026 Pyongyang International Marathon, planned for 5 April 2026, was cancelled on the decision of the DPRK Athletics Association, with no reason given. Registered runners were offered refunds. The next edition is planned for October 2027.

entries.detail: International passenger trains between Beijing and Pyongyang resumed on 12 March 2026, running four times a week via Dandong–Sinuiju, with daily Dandong–Pyongyang services. The trains carry officials and visa holders; tourist visas are still not issued to Chinese citizens.

sources.name: Yonhap News Agency
Reuters

entries.title: Beijing–Pyongyang passenger trains resume after six years

entries.detail: Air China restarted weekly Beijing–Pyongyang flights (CA121/CA122, Mondays) on 30 March 2026, six years after suspension. Air Koryo continues to serve Beijing, Shenyang and Vladivostok.

sources.name: KBS World Radio (Xinhua)
Aviation Week

entries.title: Air China resumes Beijing–Pyongyang flights

entries.detail: Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed the annual extension of the DPRK passport restriction on 2 July 2026 (Public Notice 13073, published in the Federal Register on 20 July 2026), effective 1 September 2026 through 31 August 2027.

sources.name: US Department of State — Public Notice 13073, Federal Register

entries.title: US extends passport restriction to 31 August 2027

entries.detail: The first road bridge between Russia and the DPRK — about 1 km across the Tumen River between Khasan and the Tumangang/Rason area — was inaugurated on 7 September 2026. Construction began in April 2025 under the June 2024 Putin–Kim agreement; it supplements the 1959 railway bridge.

sources.name: Nezna-io — North Korea: A Strategic Opening to China and Russia
Korea Herald

entries.title: Russia–North Korea road bridge over the Tumen River inaugurated

entries.detail: China's second bridge to Sinuiju — completed in 2014 but idle for over a decade while the North Korean-side access roads and customs facilities were unfinished — opened to traffic on 15 October 2026, adding freight capacity on the corridor that carries most China–DPRK trade.

sources.name: Nezna-io — North Korea: A Strategic Opening to China and Russia
Asian Examiner — New bridges reveal China-Russia rivalry

entries.title: New Yalu River Bridge (Dandong–Sinuiju) opens to traffic
Kim Jong Un inspects Samjiyon tourism construction — no opening announced
entries.detail: KCNA reported on 17 November 2026 that Kim Jong Un had inspected tourism construction at Samjiyon on 15–16 November: the Mount Phothae ski resort (built, unopened), a second resort under construction, Samjiyon Airport's expansion (runway extension ordered to ICAO standards) and works at the Mount Paektu summit. No opening date was announced and foreign access is unchanged: no operator sells Samjiyon and no nationality is admitted there as a tourist.

sources.name: Yonhap News Agency
The Korea Herald
